findings.evidence: Lines 17-23 (How to Apply) address employees with 'Employees must submit'; lines 25-27 (Approval Timeline) address managers with 'The manager reviews'; lines 51 (Terminology Notes) address both simultaneously with 'You record...Finance reconciles...Payroll releases.'
findings.fix: Clearly separate content by audience: create distinct sections for employee instructions and internal process documentation, or explicitly flag each section with who it is written for.
findings.location: Throughout document; most egregious in Terminology Notes (lines 49-53)
findings.violation: The document addresses multiple distinct audiences - employees, managers, finance staff, people operations - without clear separation. These audiences are interleaved throughout sections, so an employee cannot easily tell which instructions apply to them and which describe what other roles perform. The Terminology Notes section is particularly problematic, mixing employee instructions ('You record...you submit') with descriptions of internal staff actions ('Finance reconciles...Payroll releases').

findings.evidence: Line 11: 'Full-time employees...are eligible'; Line 45: 'The applicant must keep'; Line 53: 'you submit.' Also: Lines 5 and 7 introduce two different entities - 'benefits team' and 'people operations office' - that may be the same department but are never clarified.
findings.fix: Define a consistent term for each concept: choose one term for the employee reader (e.g., 'you' throughout) and one for each organization, and use only those terms throughout the document. Consider a definitions section if multiple organizations are genuinely distinct.
findings.violation: Multiple terms are used interchangeably for the same concepts without defined equivalence, forcing the reader to check whether terms refer to the same thing. Employees are variously called 'employees' (line 11), 'staff' (line 5), 'the applicant' (line 45), 'the requester' (line 29), 'the employee' (line 23), and 'you' (line 53). Organizations are called 'benefits team' (line 5), 'people operations office' (line 7), 'finance office' (line 39), 'finance liaison' (line 61), 'Finance' (line 51), and 'Payroll' (line 51) with no mapping of whether these are the same or different entities.

findings.violation: The sentence runs to 71 words with 5 subordinate-clause markers, longer than the reader can hold in mind on a single pass.
